hints.title: Child Segment In-Place Splicing
hints.text: A doubly linked list node may have a child pointing to another doubly linked list. When flattening, the child list must be spliced directly between current node and its next node.

hints.title: Recursive or Pointer Tail Splicing
hints.text: When curr has a child, find the tail of the flattened child segment. Connect curr.child to curr.next, update prev pointers, clear curr.child, and proceed.

hints.title: Iterative Pointer Rewiring
hints.text: Traverse with curr. If curr.child is present: find child tail, attach child_tail.next = curr.next (updating prev if curr.next exists), connect curr.next = curr.child and curr.child.prev = curr, set curr.child = None.

hints.title: Complete Implementation

variables: N: total number of nodes across all levels (0 <= N <= 1000)
complexity.notes: Every node is traversed a bounded number of times during splicing in-place.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Collecting nodes in an auxiliary array and rebuilding the doubly linked list requires O(N) extra memory.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: In-place pointer rewiring preserves constant auxiliary space.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Correctly updating all prev and next pointers and clearing child references to None.

solutions.approach: Iterative child tail splicing with pointer updates
